correctness.rationale: The positive weighted sequence C=Q/(1−a z^j Q) has a unique strictly dominant positive simple pole by positivity at consecutive exponents j,j+1; residue gives coefficient constant. A bivariate u marker and implicit-pole differentiation yield fixed-(a,j) mean n/L, variance nV/L^3 and Gaussian limit. Dedekind eta transformation gives log Q(e^-t)=A/t+(1/2)log(t/2π)−t/24 plus exponentially small terms. The pole equation jt=log a+log Q then gives s_gamma by a monotone root argument for a=e^{gamma sqrt(j)}, both scaled phase coefficients and dualities. Taylor expansion at t0=sqrt(A/j) gives the fixed-a log(j)/j term and amplitude. Independently solved 9 phase roots numerically. Checks support but do not substitute for eta/analytic proof.
